approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a fresh molecular graph pool from a greedily retained scored population, using rank-weighted parents, crossover and graph mutations. A Gaussian process fitted to all accepted current-session scores on count fingerprints supplies correlated function draws. The algorithm buys successive maxima of those draws, and after three non-improving batches limits eligibility to the forty highest predicted means. Canonical identity checks, the sulfur introduction rule and bounded valid fallback remain part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Replace the marginal predictive distribution with native TabICLv2 conditional quantiles and retain Gaussian-process dependence through a Gaussian copula. The quantiles determine location, width and shape together, including the mean used by the stall mask. Earlier pretrained models changed only the mean and kept an additive GP residual; sibling removals tested residual presence or correlation. This test instead asks whether a complete learned marginal law improves paid ordering while preserving dependence, with one fixed model and no tuning sweep.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent completes all15 Search cells with no posterior fallback, but half of its paid budget produces only1.0224077547621127 of5.978073077532332 total incumbent-gain mass; its mean endpoint is0.607030316211131 with seed SD0.030175277546149237. Read-only joins of4350 paid records give original-GP strict-pair accuracy0.7064888432931521 on19495 unequal-score within-batch pairs and88/435 stall-restricted batches. This supports a test of useful candidate ordering and progress magnitude, not a diagnosis that every lost opportunity is surrogate error. Both earlier pretrained-location recipes executed and worsened same-label ordering: projected TabPFNv2 .63491494 vs passiveGP .68938307 (original lock-mismatch gap preserved), and native TabPFN3.5 .65718386 vs .69824184 with matched endpoint delta-.07575616042183468 on its own older Parent. Current-host restricted/unrestricted residual removals lost .018621410181405656/.09438631107688404; restricted correlation removal lost .008352681729073996. These conditional results motivate retaining dependence but neither identify the old hybrid interaction as the cause nor establish the new quantile bridge. literature_review.conclusion: The review supports one testable different distributional mechanism, not a promise of score gain. Native source quantiles and offline loading are real APIs; full-width synthetic inference fits the issued A40 slot. Earlier TabPFN mean counterexamples and conditional dependence findings remain distinct. Preserve exact Parent lock with a tested source-equivalent adapter; retain the initial constant-column integration failure as construction evidence. Only complete paid ordering and matched endpoints can assess the scientific and performance predictions. Named normalization-group comparisons distinguish process-order reversal from numeric disagreement. Full-width eight-view inference is measured; all-constant-feature two-view stress is explicitly outside the active guard and cannot establish full-ensemble feasibility.

method_change.previous_method: Accepted-only raw-score count-Tanimoto GP Gaussian predictive marginals with correlated function sampling and stall-time mean mask.
method_change.proposed_method: Frozen native TabICLv2 conditional marginal quantiles, constant-tail inverse functions and original count-GP Gaussian copula, with the same graph search and allocation consumer.
method_change.rationale: Code Parent n-cf8d309c06de has limited late gain; old mean-only external hybrids lost ordering. Replace marginal location, scale and shape jointly while keeping existing Gaussian dependence, which has conditional retained support. This is one coordinated predictive-distribution component change, not a whole optimizer replacement or constituent attribution.

hypothesis: At each inherited refit, condition the pinned frozen TabICLv2 regressor on all chronological accepted raw scores and original2048-count rows through its exact native numerical preprocessing and target inversion, with eight fixed session-seeded none/power Latin views. Obtain ensemble-averaged raw-unit quantiles q_i,j at alpha=j/1000,j=1..999, monotonically sort only if crossing remains, and define Q_i by linear interpolation and constant tails outside[.001,.999]. Compute mu_i by exact integration of this Q, not native mean averaging or a GP blend. Retain the complete original count GP and its original successful jittered pool factor F and one original normal block N. Set d_i=sqrt(sum_j F_ij^2)>0, z=(N@F.T)/d, u=Phi(z), active_values=Q(u). Feed integrated mu to the unchanged stall eligibility consumer and active_values to the unchanged sequential first-index maxima. Original GP values remain passive; original residual magnitudes are not added to Q. The mechanism is one coordinated replacement of marginal location/scale/shape while preserving the Gaussian copula, not independent marginal sampling, another mean replacement, a kernel change or an extra ablation. Causal prediction: native quantile law changes prospective order/eligibility and paid identities, those identities enter later accepted fits/breeding, and paid strict-pair order improves; real progress and endpoint gain are separate predictions.

finding_summary.headline: The quantile–copula law ran, but paid ranking worsened and mean endpoint fell by 0.13326
finding_summary.insights: This settles the prediction that this complete marginal replacement repairs ordering on the candidates it actually buys. It also separates useful distributional coverage from useful optimization ranking: better pinball loss and broader intervals coexisted with poorer pair ordering and lower final value. The loss is not an import, checkpoint, copula-construction or unexposed-routing failure. The experiment prices the coordinated model/preprocessing/marginal/copula intervention locally; it does not isolate which of those elements caused the loss or rule out other tabular predictors. Native preprocessing retained only 296–1,318 of the 2,048 count columns, and every allocation pool varied in 200–762 columns removed as constant in the archive. This is an implemented source behavior and a plausible limitation for changing molecular pools, but its causal contribution was not isolated. A representation or surrogate that handles newly varying molecular environments is a distinct method-level hypothesis; this experiment does not establish its benefit. The molecular evidence also shows that broader generated structure is not equivalent to broader productive chemistry. The stream contained 1,733 typed scaffolds, yet each task’s thirty highest-scoring molecules occupied only 5–17. Large repeated assemblies became much more common: 571 proposals had at least 60 heavy atoms versus 22 in the Parent, while the very small tail shrank from 98 to one. The observed limitation is concentration of productive search within a few recurring families amid extensive scaffold elaboration, not literal single-scaffold collapse. A search scheme or proposal operator that maintains alternative ring/linker families and ordinary attachment environments could address that separate limitation; no universal size cutoff or causal explanation of this surrogate’s loss follows. The measured result leaves those alternatives, calibrated noiseless uncertainty and the broader approach open, while preserving the earlier interventions’ verdicts.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches executed the registered eight-view quantile law and inherited Gaussian dependence without fallback. Every batch changed its paid set: 2,819 of 4,350 purchased identities were absent from the same-state GP batch. On those exact purchased labels, strict-pair accuracy fell from 70.83% for the passive GP to 67.91% for the active integrated means (19,450 unequal-score pairs); it worsened in 13 of 15 task/seed cells, tied in one and improved in one. This triggers the registered ordering falsifier. Distributional prediction nevertheless improved on the secondary pinball measure, from 0.014931 to 0.013671, with broader intervals and higher coverage; mean-squared error worsened from 0.004574 to 0.004884. Changed choices entered subsequent fits and breeding, so the routing effect was exposed rather than merely logged. The mean endpoint was 0.473773 versus the Parent/Anchor’s 0.607030, a paired decrease of 0.133258; all three seed macros and 12 of 15 task endpoints declined. Population seed dispersion increased from 0.030175 to 0.038651. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.978073 to 3.979211 over 4,350 purchases, although gain in the final 2,175 purchases rose from 1.022408 to 1.763311. Thus stronger late recovery did not recover the lost full-budget result. The complete matched +0.002 criterion was missed, and the protocol’s paired task-safety test identified a material regression on sitagliptin_mpo.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and enlarged scaffold assemblies; reactive substituents and undefined stereochemistry remain common
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 are covered: 870 evaluated optimizer proposals per objective, with initial observations kept separate. context.comparison reports both child_complete and paired_complete true against code Parent n-cf8d309c06de; all supplied Child and published Parent trajectory files exist and were read. These are mostly neutral, highly substituted aromatic or partially saturated heterocycles carrying carbonyls, ethers, amines and halogens, with sulfur chemistry concentrated in one output family. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9931 to 1.0 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.7402 to 1.0; these are molecule-level SMILES string flags, not fractions of atoms or perceived aromatic ring counts. RDKit perception separately confirms extensive ring chemistry. Size is heterogeneous: 571 of 4350 Child proposals have at least 60 heavy atoms versus 22 Parent proposals, while only 1 has at most 6 versus 98 in the Parent. Neither larger nor smaller is universally better in these trajectories. Repeated heteroaromatic units, enlarged nitrogen rings, fused cages, N-halogen bonds and peroxides coexist with ordinary medicinal-chemistry-like scaffolds. There are 334 N-halogen and 75 O-halogen-bearing proposals, lower than Parent 888 and 162, but peroxide-bearing proposals increase to 396 from 118. These are presence counts, not bond counts. Carbon polyhalogenation occurs in 75 Child and 24 Parent proposals, so this capability is not absent. No Child proposal has a formally charged atom, and no perceived tetrahedral center is assigned; 2469 proposals have at least one unassigned tetrahedral center. Net-neutrality was measured separately and is not being used to infer the absence of charged atoms. Basic neutral amines are present; lack of formal charge is not lack of ionizable nitrogen. Synthesis, chemical stability, protonation at assay conditions and biological usefulness were not measured. Broad full-stream structural coverage contracts into a few recurring leader families; scaffold counts describe graph coverage, not chemical feasibility. Evidence: policy/requests/r0062-03-improve-L01-molecular-assess-3b653ebb1382ad30.json; policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/input-manifest.json; policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json. The manifest lists every underlying trajectory file and original trusted path with SHA256. The Child snapshots are byte-identical preservation copies; only the frozen digest/trusted paths authorize cited SMILES. All derived counts use evaluated optimizer rows only. High/low cohorts mean ten highest/lowest recorded scores within each seed, pooled to thirty per objective; they are descriptive, with evaluation order breaking score ties. The audits do not cover rejected or unpurchased internal candidates, establish synthetic routes, attribute chemistry to a component, or decide mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact indole-like carboxamides and fused aza-aromatic carbonyl compounds decorated with methoxy/ethoxy, alkyl and halogen groups. The 870 optimizer molecules span 9-50 heavy atoms, median 25; median perceived ring and aromatic-ring counts are both 3. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 293, score 0.4711064141789182, is a 24-heavy-atom fused aza-aromatic aryl ketone with ethoxy, methyl, amino and aryl fluoride substituents. It contains no amide or N-halogen bond. Seed 1 instead reaches 0.46092619585962435 with a brominated indole carboxamide bearing N-Br; seed 2 reaches 0.42762099872850584 with an N-fluorinated indole carboxamide and aminomethyl group. The ketone leader is comparatively conventional, whereas N-halogenated analogues deserve chemical-stability scrutiny. Parent seed maxima are 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554: the Child retains similar compact aromatic families and does not improve every seed. The final seed-2 molecule, score 0.3726558544705772, still has an N-F indole, chloromethyl ether and thioamide. Chemistry audits: policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json, policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json, policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json. Each audit cites the underlying Child trajectory snapshot and published Parent trajectory by individual run-relative file and SHA256.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 120 proposals; 14 have O-halogen bonds and 14 have peroxide bonds. High score does not establish their stability.
45 proposals have a perceived ring of four or fewer atoms made entirely of aromatic atoms; this is a structural flag requiring geometry review, not a proved synthesis impossibility.
missing_features: Broader exploration of compact fused aza-aromatic carbonyl arrangements is limited among the leaders; the best seed-0 ketone supplies an observed alternative to the recurring indole-carboxamide family.

Chemically ordinary attachment environments are not consistently retained while altering substitution. No unique absent required pharmacophore or benefit from formal charge can be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The higher thirty have 23-26 heavy atoms and median 3 rings; the lower thirty have median 40 heavy atoms and 5 rings. The lowest cited molecule is an extensively linked polyaryl/thioamide assembly scoring 2.636351280349585e-22, compared with the compact aryl ketone at 0.4711064141789182. This supports a local preference for compact heteroaromatic carbonyl arrangements over indiscriminate scaffold concatenation. It does not isolate a ketone, amide, halogen or specific nitrogen as a causal reward feature: 15 of the higher thirty still contain N-halogen bonds. There are 237 typed Murcko scaffolds in the full stream but only 7 among the higher thirty.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest output family: 24-120 heavy atoms, median 56, with median 8 rings and 8 perceived aromatic rings. Linked and fused aza-aromatics carry esters, ethers, carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles and repeated scaffold units. 405 of 870 molecules have at least 60 heavy atoms, compared with 10 Parent molecules; Parent median heavy atoms is 32. The seed-0 leader is a 72-heavy-atom, 12-ring assembly containing several related carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, scoring 0.5974313551815766. Seed 1 reaches 0.6338235294117647 with a 47-heavy-atom ester-decorated aza-aromatic assembly containing a cyclic cumulated carbon-double-bond segment. Seed 2 reaches 0.6112400363232772 with a polyheteroaromatic hydrazine-linked, carbonyl-containing structure bearing vinyl ether substitution. These graphs are diverse but many would require demanding syntheses and structural verification. The corresponding Parent maxima are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496; the Parent leaders also contain questionable reactive or strained motifs. The last seed-0 and seed-2 records retain their respective leader-family scores, illustrating late peripheral analogues rather than a clean change of chemical family. Chemistry audits: policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json, policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json, policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json. Each audit cites the underlying Child trajectory snapshot and published Parent trajectory by individual run-relative file and SHA256.
liabilities: Large repeated ring assemblies and ester-rich branches create substantial synthetic and conformational burden; the broad heavy-atom tail is a measured feature, not a universal size cutoff recommendation.

17 proposals contain carbon-carbon cumulated double bonds, including 5 of the higher thirty; 104 have peroxide bonds, including 4 of the higher thirty. A generic double-bond flag was not used to identify these motifs.
missing_features: Compact decorated nitrogen-containing cores that combine the observed ring/acceptor arrangements without extensive scaffold duplication are underrepresented among Child leaders relative to the Parent comparison.

Ordinary ring connectivity that preserves those arrangements is not consistently retained: the best Child family includes cyclic cumulative unsaturation. The score does not identify a single missing functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The lowest optimizer example is a partially dearomatized ester/phenol-linked carbonyl heterocycle at 0.528153827722535; the maximum is 0.6338235294117647. The initial-record minimum of 0.5 is not an optimizer result. The higher and lower thirty both include ten molecules with at least 60 heavy atoms, and their heavy-atom medians are 46.5 and 51.5. Thus size alone does not explain the local gradient. The visible association is with arrangement and repetition of decorated nitrogen-containing ring systems, including unusual ring expansions, rather than with general makeability. The broad 526 typed-scaffold stream narrows to 11 in the higher thirty; the strongest Parent seed achieves a higher recorded score with a much smaller structure, but this is not a matched size intervention.

per_task.generated_character: Halogenated aromatic structures connected to partially saturated amine rings, phenols, sulfur-oxygen groups and amide side chains dominate. There are 13-119 heavy atoms per proposal, median 39, with median 5 rings and 3 aromatic rings; 135 molecules have at least 60 heavy atoms versus 10 in the Parent. Seed 0 reaches 0.7406513372419333 with a halogenated, amino-rich diaryl structure containing a bridged oxygen ring. Seed 1 reaches 0.9767993639759021 with a 36-heavy-atom, six-ring cage/fused assembly containing tertiary cyclic amines, phenol, bromine/chlorine and a sulfoxide side chain. Seed 2 reaches only 0.311587596471083 with a 35-heavy-atom aminoamide/sulfone-bearing structure carrying an aryl hydroperoxide. Parent maxima are 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864. Their leaders are smaller amine-bearing aromatic systems, though some have strained rings or aminal centers themselves. The seed-2 final molecule remains in its hydroperoxide/aminoamide family and scores 0.16571080479827865. Chemistry audits: policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-drd2_docking.json, policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-drd2_docking.json, policy/scratch/r0062-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-drd2_docking.json. Each audit cites the underlying Child trajectory snapshot and published Parent trajectory by individual run-relative file and SHA256.
liabilities: 146 proposals contain peroxide bonds and 8 of the higher thirty do; the seed-2 leader explicitly contains an aryl hydroperoxide.

The most decorated cage-like leader has multiple unassigned stereogenic centers and a sulfoxide; its graph and score alone do not establish accessible stereochemistry, stability or synthetic feasibility.
Very large halogenated structures and densely substituted amino centers coexist with comparatively ordinary amine scaffolds; size and nitrogen counts alone cannot diagnose the score.
missing_features: Consistent coverage of compact aromatic/amine arrangements is missing across sessions; such chemistry is demonstrably producible, but one seed remains in an aminoamide/sulfone/hydroperoxide family.

Assigned configurations are absent despite all thirty high-score molecules having unassigned tetrahedral centers. The trajectories contain no stereoisomer or protonation comparison establishing that either would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low N-chloro amide attached to an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine scores 0.00016650955053713697, and the small aryl sulfonate ester scores 0.00024675866379847753. All thirty high-score molecules contain a conservative structural amine-candidate motif, versus eight of the lower thirty; this query excludes amide/sulfonamide and aryl-attached nitrogen and is not a pKa calculation. 18 of the lower thirty contain direct sulfonamide bonds, compared with none of the higher thirty. The observable association favors available aliphatic amine environments together with aromatic shape, rather than just sulfonylated nitrogen. This is not proof of binding or a universal anti-sulfur rule. Only 5 typed scaffolds occur among the higher thirty despite 334 across the full stream, and the pooled best conceals strong seed-to-seed chemical differences.

per_task.generated_character: The recurring chemistry combines two aryl regions with unsaturated, nitrogen-containing fused or enlarged rings, lactam/carbonyl groups, N-methyl substitution, and alkoxy/alkyl groups. The full stream spans 4-70 heavy atoms, median 35, with median 4 rings and 2 aromatic rings. Seed 0 reaches 0.2225098886497406 with a 36-heavy-atom diaryl fused/enlarged nitrogen-ring structure containing an amide carbonyl and a ketone. Seed 1 reaches 0.2133584675546675 with a bridged polyheterocycle containing an N-N linkage, imine, ethoxy and carbonyl groups. Seed 2 reaches 0.22020415990760814 with another 36-heavy-atom diaryl nitrogen-ring/carbonyl structure. Parent maxima are 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313; Parent leader heavy-atom counts are 34, 30 and 31. Familiar functional groups are combined in unusually fused or enlarged ring topologies whose syntheses and stereochemical accessibility remain uncertain. Final molecules stay within these families; the last seed-2 record scores 0.20100756305184245. liabilities: Ring enlargement and bridge formation create multiple stereogenic and potentially conformationally demanding structures without assigned configuration.
100 proposals contain peroxide bonds, although none of the higher thirty do; 30 proposals have at least 60 heavy atoms and 15 of these occur in the lower thirty.
One late proposal is the four-heavy-atom CCCF fragment; it is an isolated residual of the small-molecule tail, not the dominant Child output.
missing_features: Leader coverage of more compact arrangements of the existing aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl features is limited relative to the Parent. The comparison does not reveal one necessary absent substituent.

Configurable stereochemistry and better coverage of alternative ring topologies are missing from the observed leader families; every high-cohort molecule has an unassigned tetrahedral center, with no measured stereochemical reward comparison.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The acyclic fragment CCCF scores 0.01894972862287957; a much larger duplicated carbonyl-rich heteroaromatic assembly scores 0.11034490710549984. The higher thirty occupy 34-38 heavy atoms, compared with median 59 among the lower thirty; all thirty high molecules contain an amide motif and two aryl regions are common. This supports a local balance of aromatic placement, nitrogen-ring topology and carbonyl arrangement rather than either deletion to fragments or duplication of whole scaffolds. A methyl-bearing leader and its thiol-bearing analogue tie exactly at 0.2225098886497406, so that side-group replacement supplies no evidence of a new score-relevant feature. There are 17 typed scaffolds among the higher thirty versus 22 in the Parent higher thirty; the Child does not literally collapse to a single scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The three sessions produce markedly different families: a heavily bridged nonaromatic nitrogen/carbonyl cage, a simpler substituted benzamide/ketone, and fluorinated carbonyl-rich fused nitrogen heterocycles. Across 870 proposals the heavy-atom range is 9-60, median 28; median rings is 4 and median aromatic rings is 1. Seed 0 reaches 0.4746557230814677 with a seven-ring nonaromatic cage carrying fluoromethyl groups, carbonyls, a hydroxyl group and an N-S bond. Seed 1 reaches 0.21976588771462166 with a 20-heavy-atom aminoaryl benzamide bearing vinylamido, vinyl ether and fluoromethyl-ketone features. Seed 2 reaches 0.524911241687462 with a 30-heavy-atom fused nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycle, N-O-aryl linkage and gem-difluorocyclobutenyl amino substituent. The latter establishes actual carbon polyfluorination, not just isolated aryl fluorides. Parent maxima are 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813, with different fluorinated nitrogen-ring arrangements and their own N-halogen/strained-ring liabilities. The final seed-2 molecule substitutes N-Cl/N-F environments and scores 0.10108320894433159; the last molecule is not the incumbent. Each audit cites the underlying Child trajectory snapshot and published Parent trajectory by individual run-relative file and SHA256.
liabilities: 114 proposals contain N-halogen bonds, 32 peroxide bonds, and 25 a small all-aromatic perceived ring. Carbon polyhalogenation occurs in 56 proposals and is therefore not an absent capability.
The gem-difluorocyclobutene and the seven-ring cage raise different strain and synthesis questions; the nonaromatic cage leader has four unassigned tetrahedral centers.
N-O-aryl and N-S linkages, vinyl ethers, and unusual bridge connectivity require chemical review; no measured stability or synthesis evidence is available.
missing_features: Consistent access to compact fluorinated nitrogen-containing ring arrangements is missing across seeds; the capability exists in one session but the others follow distinct cage and simple aromatic families.

Stable-looking attachment environments that retain the higher-scoring carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement are not consistently explored: N-halogen variants and complex cages remain prominent. The evidence does not establish a uniquely missing target-specific motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Large linked carbonyl-rich polyheteroaromatics occupy the extreme low tail, including the cited 4.47088300341386e-54 example. The higher thirty have median 28 heavy atoms versus 49 for the lower thirty; fluorinated, more compact nitrogen-containing structures are associated with higher scores here. All thirty higher molecules have a perceived carbon-carbon double bond, which includes cyclic alkenes and should not be confused with generic carbonyl unsaturation. Replacing one N-methyl of the best fused dicarbonyl scaffold with N-F gives the observed 0.487229171931783 analogue, below 0.524911241687462; later N-Br and multiple N-halogen variants are also weaker. These comparisons do not identify a universally beneficial fluorination pattern or prove a missing known reference structure. Ten of the higher thirty still have N-halogen bonds. Only 8 typed scaffolds remain among the higher thirty out of 327 in the full stream.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In node n-16b934239c55 under the frozen three-seed Search panel, 334 of 4350 evaluated proposals have N-halogen bonds, 75 have O-halogen bonds and 396 have peroxide bonds. The paired Parent counts are 888, 162 and 118. Some such motifs survive into the highest-score cohorts, while other leaders contain none. The counts support a remaining chemical-environment gap, not a claim that every liability became more frequent or caused the score outcome.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry does not consistently preserve ordinary local bonding environments while retaining useful scaffold features.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic chemistry intervention could make edits aware of attachment atom and local reactivity, preserving alternative ordinary bonding environments around the same scaffold. Any proposed constraint needs a separate controlled test: structural flags are not measured instability, and the current predictive intervention does not identify which generator component is responsible.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The current Search stream contains 74 molecules with a perceived ring of four or fewer entirely aromatic atoms, and 17 with carbon-carbon cumulated double bonds. Five members of one high-score cohort contain the latter motif. Multi-bridged cages and enlarged nitrogen rings also occur among leaders. These are explicit graph features, not a proof that every flagged structure is impossible to synthesize.
transferable_gaps.gap: Access to rings is abundant, but ordinary ring geometry is not reliably retained during scaffold elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general ring-editing capability could distinguish routine fusion, bridging and ring expansion from geometrically demanding closures, and make less strained alternative connectivities available. Preserve this as a chemistry hypothesis conditioned on these emitted molecules; it does not establish an optimal ring-size rule or a causal component failure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4350 Child proposals, charged-atom incidence and assigned tetrahedral-center incidence are both zero; 2469 molecules have at least one unassigned tetrahedral center. Neutral amine candidates are common, and high-score cyclic amines, sulfoxide-containing cages and enlarged nitrogen rings expose configurational ambiguity. No alternative charge state or assigned stereoisomer was compared.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not express assigned tetrahedral configuration or formal charge states despite generating stereogenic and ionizable structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and candidate generation could support chemically appropriate stereochemical and ionization alternatives while respecting canonical identity and only current-session feedback. This is missing representational coverage, not evidence that a particular charge or configuration improves an objective; neutral amines must not be mistaken for an absence of basic centers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child has 571 proposals with at least 60 heavy atoms versus 22 in the paired Parent, but only 1 at most 6 heavy atoms versus 98. Two output families contain 405 and 135 large-tail proposals. Several leader families are much more compact than their lowest-score scaffold concatenations, while another objective has large molecules in both high and low cohorts. Thus neither blanket shrinking nor blanket growth follows from these observations.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold elaboration does not reliably balance compact chemical alternatives against repetition of whole ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could preserve multiple size and connectivity alternatives when joining or elaborating scaffolds, using session feedback to decide which survive. Any control should keep both molecular size tails visible and test useful progress without prescribing a universal heavy-atom floor, ceiling, or causal explanation for this Child.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Full-stream typed Murcko scaffold counts range from 237 to 526 across the five outputs, but the pooled thirty highest-score molecules contain only 5 to 17. Exact score ties occur for methyl/thiol substitutions, ester-chain variants and other peripheral changes. Some paired seeds produce compact amine or fluorinated heterocycle families while others remain in quite different chemistry. These are trajectory associations; neither single-scaffold collapse nor a breeding mechanism attribution is established.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph variation does not consistently translate into multiple productive chemical families within a session.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to alternative ring/linker arrangements and distinguish peripheral analogues from substantive scaffold changes using task-agnostic structural descriptions and current-session feedback. Treat chemical-family coverage as a testable search capability, not a hardcoded target scaffold, a guaranteed benefit from diversity, or transferable credit to a specific component.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
